clue.text: Porgy and Bess composer in his blue period

definitions.text: Porgy and Bess composer in his blue period

parts.words: Porgy and Bess composer in his blue period
parts.note: Gershwin, who wrote Porgy and Bess, also wrote Rhapsody in Blue, so in that 'blue period' he was a writer of rhapsodies

explanation.surface: An art-history style note on Gershwin going through a melancholy blue phase, like Picasso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue period' borrows Picasso's phrase; the real point is Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue, which made him a composer of rhapsodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes rhapsodies, as Gershwin did with Rhapsody in Blue, is a composer of that musical form.

clue.text: Headstrong, goes right to the top of the tree

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece placed at the top comes first, above the rest

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: An impetuous person rushes to climb to the treetop.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting impetuously without thought means being reckless.

clue.text: Offhand it seems a first rate transport system

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as the letters A and I
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A passenger casually remarks that a rail network appears excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 meaning first-rate is written with a capital I standing for the figure one; 'it seems' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual, nonchalant manner is light and breezy.

clue.text: Marksman's first attempt at positioning, say

definitions.text: Marksman's first attempt at positioning, say

parts.words: Marksman's first attempt at positioning, say
parts.note: a trial round fired to check where a rifle's aim falls, so the shooter can adjust the gun's alignment

explanation.surface: A shooter's opening try at getting into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Positioning' hints at the shooter's own stance, but it is the adjusting of the gunsights.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial round fired to adjust a gun's aiming device is a marksman's opening attempt.

clue.text: Thomas embarrasses lady over a point

indicators.note: to embarrass is to put into disorder or confusion, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: N, for north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A man named Thomas makes a woman blush over some small matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrasses' rearranges LADY, then N follows; 'over a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh poet Thomas, author of Under Milk Wood, had this first name.

clue.text: Sounds very eager to support sin in a place of worship

indicators.note: sounds signals that the words are read by how they would be said, not how they are spelt

parts.note: agog means very eager; placed under sin in a down answer it gives sin agog

explanation.surface: Someone keen to back wrongdoing turns up in a house of prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts AGOG under SIN in a down entry, and SIN AGOG said quickly gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish house of prayer and study is a building for worship.

clue.text: Bird gets a single encore

parts.note: a single thing is one, the Roman numeral I
bis is the French and musical call for an encore, meaning twice

explanation.surface: A bird is called back for a solo repeat performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading bird, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Mr Harding's home, serving up shellfish to Lady Stanhope

indicators.note: in a down clue, serving up means the word is written upwards, reversing it

parts.note: a crab is a shellfish
Lady Hester Stanhope was a famous English traveller in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone dishes up seafood to a titled lady at a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Harding is the clergyman of Trollope's The Warden, set in this fictional cathedral city; 'serving up' turns CRAB upwards to make BARC.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope set his novel about the warden Septimus Harding in this cathedral city, home of his Barsetshire clergy.

clue.text: Jack takes monkeys up, see, one by one

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are written from the bottom, reversing them

parts.note: jack and tar are both slang for a sailor
apes are monkeys, loosely
Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A sailor carries some monkeys upstairs and points them out individually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TAR plus APES upwards together, giving SEPARAT; then comes ELY, the bishop's see in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking things individually, apart from each other, is dealing with them singly.

clue.text: Horses in training include a child's horse with learner going off course

indicators.note: the string of horses wraps around the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a string is the set of racehorses kept at one trainer's stable
gee-gee is nursery language for a horse, shortened to GG
L is the learner sign on British practice cars

explanation.surface: A stable's racehorses take in a pony and a novice rider who wanders off the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts A, GG and L inside STRING, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying and wandering away from the line or group means drifting from the route.

clue.text: Corn perhaps associated with the neck

definitions.meaning: a harvest of grain such as corn
the pouch in a bird's gullet, found in its neck, where food is stored

explanation.definitionFit: A harvest of cereal is the farming sense; the bird's throat pouch for storing food is the anatomical one.

clue.text: He rambled along erratically, selling his songs

definitions.text: He rambled along erratically, selling his songs

indicators.note: something done erratically follows no fixed pattern, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wandering minstrel strolled about hawking his tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a travelling seller of ballads and also supplies the letters, RAMBLED ALONG rearranged by 'erratically'.
explanation.definitionFit: A street seller of printed ballad sheets, later a contemptuous word for a poor poet, wandered from town to town.

clue.text: Her office job makes her parents go wild

indicators.note: going wild means behaving in a disordered way, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl's choice of clerical work drives her mother and father to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges HER PARENTS GO; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shorthand typist was the classic office post for a secretary taking dictation.

clue.text: Foolish goat!

parts.note: silly means foolish
a billy is a male goat

explanation.surface: Someone calls another person a stupid goat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'goat' is also slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An affectionate term for a foolish person, as one might mildly scold someone acting the goat.

clue.text: Colourful smell of beer after work

indicators.note: the smell of beer comes after work, so that piece follows in the answer

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
ale is beer and its scent is its smell, together read as the beer's smell

explanation.surface: Someone describes a vivid whiff of ale after the working day.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing a milky shifting play of rainbow hues, like an opal, is a vivid, many-hued effect.

clue.text: In one finish Redcap looks threatening

indicators.note: the Redcap is placed in the middle of the other pieces, which enclose it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an ending is a finish or conclusion
a Redcap is a British military policeman, so MP for Military Police

explanation.surface: A military policeman appears menacing at the end of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cap covers they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen, usually unpleasant, looms like a menace.

clue.text: All the batsmen dismissed-everted

definitions.meaning: the batting team, the side that is in, has been bowled out
turned so that the inner surface faces outward

explanation.definitionFit: Read as cricket, the batting team is all out; as a phrase it means turned with the inner surface outward.

clue.text: Hungarian 1 ac

parts.note: the composer of the Hungarian Rhapsodies, read with the answer to 1 across as a Hungarian composer of rhapsodies

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking for a Hungarian version of the first across answer.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' points to 1 across; the Hungarian Rhapsodies make this composer a Hungarian of that kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian piano virtuoso wrote nineteen Hungarian Rhapsodies, so he was a rhapsodist from Hungary.

clue.text: Starts to lie on long lounge' so

definitions.text: Starts to lie on long lounge' so

indicators.note: starts of words are their opening letters, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone begins to stretch out on a long sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the starts of 'lie on long lounge so' spell the answer, and the clue describes the lazy sprawling it means.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl idly and lazily is to lounge around, as the clue's picture of lying on a long sofa shows.

clue.text: Veronica's magic formula brought about weed destruction

definitions.note: Veronica's is read as Veronica is

indicators.note: brought about means put around, so the spell is wrapped round the other letters

parts.note: a spell is a magic formula of words

indicators.note: destruction wrecks the word weed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Veronica uses a charm to kill off garden weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica looks like a woman's name but is the botanical name of a plant. 'brought about' puts EEDW (WEED rearranged by 'destruction') inside SPELL, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant genus Veronica is commonly called by this name, a small blue-flowered herb.

clue.text: "Op inside" says one in charge of a band of travellers ?

definitions.text: "Op inside" says one in charge of a band of travellers ?

parts.words: "Op inside" says one in charge of a band of travellers ?
parts.note: the one in charge of a band sounds like a music director, but the band is passengers and the call is a dropped-h 'hop inside' from a London double-decker's ticket collector

explanation.surface: A bandleader shouts a cryptic instruction to a touring group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: British buses once carried a ticket collector who called 'hop inside'; 'band' and 'one in charge' make it look like a music conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticket collector on a British bus directed the passengers, as a conductor directs musicians.

clue.text: One's embraced by that French girl

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so the one goes within the French word

parts.note: cela is French for that
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone is hugged by a French girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts I inside CELA, the French for 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, used in Shakespeare's As You Like It.

clue.text: An employee's cards?

definitions.meaning: a worker, as in a farm worker or a ship's crew member
the set of playing cards dealt to one player

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is'; the question mark flags the pun on a worker being handed his cards, British slang for being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker on a farm or ship is called this, and the same word means the cards dealt to one player.

clue.text: The lady's love, no doubt

parts.note: her means belonging to a lady
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman's sweetheart, surely.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a heroine's beloved is the main man of the story; 'no doubt' marks the definition as a fair guess.
explanation.definitionFit: In a romance the leading man, the champion she adores, is the object of the heroine's affection.

clue.text: Welsh diet forcibly fed to Pistol

definitions.text: Welsh diet forcibly fed to Pistol

parts.words: Welsh diet forcibly fed to Pistol
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Henry V the Welsh captain Fluellen makes the braggart Pistol eat the Welsh national vegetable

explanation.surface: A firearm is stuffed with Welsh food, as if a gun could eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is a character in Shakespeare's Henry V, not a gun; Fluellen forces him to eat this vegetable, a Welsh emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: This onion-like vegetable is the Welsh national emblem, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Like Eton (but not Harrow) and certain churches

definitions.meaning: Eton is officially Eton College while Harrow is Harrow School, two famous English private boarding schools
describing a church run by a chapter of canons rather than a bishop, such as Westminster Abbey

explanation.definitionFit: The word means having the character of a college, as Eton does, and names churches endowed with a chapter of canons.

clue.text: Nevertheless one may be found in the Himalayas

definitions.text: Nevertheless one may be found in the Himalayas

parts.note: yet means nevertheless or even so
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Even so, a single specimen might turn up in the high mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the creature is said to live in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of legend is supposed to roam the high Himalayan snows.

clue.text: Can it give us morning tea with the early news?

definitions.text: Can it give us morning tea with the early news?

parts.words: Can it give us morning tea with the early news?
parts.note: a joking question whether a set powered by steam could brew tea as well as broadcast the morning bulletin

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a bedside gadget could make tea while playing the morning bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a jokey name for old-fashioned sound broadcasting, as opposed to television; the clue pretends the steam could boil a kettle.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular term for traditional sound broadcasting once television took over, as if powered by a steam engine.
